blurb: British flushing spaniel with sharply divided show and field lines, a top sniffer dog
description: The English Springer Spaniel is a medium-sized British gundog with a feathered liver or black and white coat, bred to flush and retrieve game.
answer: The English Springer Spaniel is a British gun dog traditionally used to flush, or spring, and retrieve game. It is a medium-sized, compact dog, and the UK breed standard calls for a height of about 51 cm. It is widely used as a sniffer dog, and its show and working lines look almost like different breeds.

body: John Caius described spaniels in 1576, and by 1801 land spaniels were being split into springing and cocking types. For a long time cockers and springers came from the same litters: the smaller dogs hunted woodcock while the larger ones flushed game birds for falcons or hawks. The breed descends from the Norfolk and Shropshire spaniels of the mid-19th century. The Kennel Club recognized it as a distinct breed in 1902, and the American Kennel Club followed in 1910.

The Springer is compact and balanced, with a gentle expression and a moderately long coat feathered on the legs and tail. Colors include black or liver with white, blue or liver roan, and tricolor with tan markings. Show dogs have longer coats, more pendulous ears and heavier bone, while field-bred dogs are wiry with shorter, coarser coats. The two gene pools have been almost completely separate for at least 70 years.

Sources describe the Springer mainly through its work: field dogs are selected for scenting ability, hunting skill and response to training. Its willingness to work is cited as the reason it is favored by search and rescue teams.

As a working gundog, the Springer is generally expected to need regular exercise and an outlet for its nose. The coat sheds mainly in spring and summer. The breed is used to detect explosives, drugs and other targets in many countries.

Conditions reported in the breed include several skin conditions such as Malassezia dermatitis, otitis externa and primary seborrhoea, as well as hip dysplasia and chronic hepatitis. A survey of UK breed club members found cancer the most common cause of death. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.5 years, and a 2022 study found 11.92 years.

faq.q: How big does an English Springer Spaniel get?
faq.a: The UK breed standard calls for about 51 cm at the withers. Show-line males usually weigh 18 to 27 kg, and working types can be lighter.

faq.q: How long do English Springer Spaniels live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.5 years, and a 2022 UK study found 11.92 years.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Springer and a Cocker Spaniel?
faq.a: The Springer is larger, with shorter, higher-set ears, a longer muzzle and a less abundant coat than the English Cocker.
